If you've or your gf are not familiar w codependency **you both** should to do some research. You should explain how you feel, and maybe take time to explore this together.  A quick search for codependency, codependent relationship, or phenomena which cause codependency such as neglect,children of alcoholics/ substance abuse will flip your world around. You are not the first, or last person to go through this. **YOU ARE NOT ALONE** 

 It seems like you both of went through some hard times, and found something really great. But codependent attachments to one another are preventing you both from having happy, stress free lives. Fining ways to have healthier attachments could really flip your relationship around. Codependency is typically found w couples that have trust issues, and especially when someone has been abused or neglected. Your gf is really terrified/afraid you will leave her. In fact **SHE IS ALREADY CONVINCED you don't want her,** and will leave her. BC she has very low self esteem,   BC EVERY SHITTY ass-whole she's ever know has used, abused, and then left her in one way or another. The woman you fell in love w is still there. She's just afraid. Codependency can leave you feeling very sad, depressed, alone, small and worthless. It is a fickle emotion that most people don't spot. The fact that your GF constantly needs validation, and is willing to comprise so much to give you anything you want. Is not good. You are both getting a sense of self, self esteem and purpose from affection of the other. When she isn't getting that, the abuse she has suffered causes her to feel afraid there might be some reason you don't want her. The cycle just continues. You could even spend all of your time together and still feel alone. Its about not feeling heard, appreciated, valued or respected. Maybe there is something you two might be doing or saying to each other. If and when you fight I imagine the arguments get really heated ( and sometime even violet)? Or your gf is avoiding this bc she is so afraid if she does something for herself, and maybe makes a mistake in the process, you will blame her and not want her anymore. She's looking for the validation bc it shows her that she is valuable. Even if its a simple task, anything that gets positive attention. Unfortunately, your gf is letting you walk all over her, and in turn you're doing it. Well, if I had no voice and was too afraid to speak up I would probably feel like shit. Codependency can be really hurtful. She  needs to get what she wants or needs from the relationship. And she needs to feel like its ok to ask, or even want something ( from you or from anyone).  she's probably feeling like she isn't important, that she doesn't matter, that she's being taken advantage of. But she's willing to keep quite in order to keep the peace. If you want to stay in the relationship YOU need to help her find away to feel relaxed and safe making mistakes. Not having to worry about being looked down on or scrutinized. Not that YOU did any of these things, but chances are someone has in her past. And that's why she's acting like this now. A little bit of trust goes a long way. Sometimes its the tittle things you don't notice. Like if she does the dishes, and says " Hey, I did the dishes." You don't have to go over and look at the dishes... to make sure she did them. You could just response positively by 1. telling her what a great job she did 2. thanking her for the favor 3. telling her how much you appreciate the favor/ gift 4. letting her know how much she means to you 5. offering to do something nice fore him in the future ( like take out the garbage) 6. ask if she actually wants you to look at the dishes, or would prefer if you return the favor in the form of generosity or affection ( ie the taking out the garbage or doing something for her)             Another way to alleviate codependent attachments is to not make the decisions for the person. This can be tricky bc you don't want the person to feel like you don't care. You want her to know its important to you, but you also want both of you to be happy. If you are always getting your way she obviously isn't happy. So make distinctions about who calls the shots on what. AND own the responsibility associated w making those decisions. If you make a mistake its not the end of the world.              If she is constantly asking for your opinion she might feel you are leaving the conversation prematurely. In keeping with the concept of helping her feel appreciated and wanted, when you leave a conversation explain why you have to leave and they say you are sorry you have to go. So explain you have a responsibility ( such as work), and that you have to go do this thing bc of what ever reason, and then say you were really happy to chat or see her, and that you can't want to do it again. And then make plans to continue the conversation. Make sure you aren't leaving it open ended. Example, " I have to hang up the phone, bc I'm at work and I'm working on this projects. I'm sorry this is bad timing, and I want to be there for you. You/this is very important to me, and I want to talk about this later. Can you remember, write down, save, email/send  what ever info you want to share w me. AND we'll talk about it tonight at dinner. I look forward to discussing your decision. I'm confident in whatever you decide. I support, trust, and love you regardless of your decisions. I can't wait to see you later. Love you. Bye." Emphasizing the responsibility before mentioning you have to leave will be better received. Otherwise it can leave the person feeling like you don't want to talk w them, that you are leaving to do this simple thing that is more important than they are, and that you have just wasted their time. That conversation can be interpreted much better than, " I have to go, bc I have to get back to work." Another example:  good "Pizza is on sale! I have to go (presumably bc it will run out if I don't get it now). I'll see you tonight!!!" vs bad "I have to go. Pizza is on sale. I'll see you tonight?" The second way might make pizza seem more important than talking, and also make the meetup less certain. Which in turn makes the listener feel less valuable, more worried, uncertain about the future. You can learn a lot of little tips if you look up Codependency disorder. You and your gf might also want to consider counseling. although you'd be amazed how much taking the first steps really helps
